value: fewer flying adult Manx shearwaters over the colony during experimental light-on periods, with a stronger effect under green and blue than under red light; the abstract also gives stronger effects at higher intensity and longer light-on periods
units: categorical (change in number of birds in flight)
eye: adult birds in flight, whole animal
method: field experiment on Skomer Island, Wales: a torch with gel filters (blue, green, red, dimmed white, bright white) placed next to a thermal camera, one minute light-on and one minute light-off per pair (two minutes of darkness for controls); birds in flight 5-85 m from the camera counted by MATLAB motion tracking
conditions: wild breeding colony, 20 nights between 14 June and 14 August 2018 (10 nights each for the spectra and interval experiments); spectra experiment at two sites (the Farm and the Neck), interval experiment at the Neck on nights with no visible moon; 81-88 light/dark pairs per colour and 86 control pairs; order of settings chosen each day with a constrained randomised design (each of six settings used 10 times over two hours, none repeated more than twice in a row); the counts are of unmarked flying adults, the authors say some birds may have passed more than once, and ages and sexes are not given. Sources were not intensity-matched: radiant flux was measured as 1.4 W (blue, 450 nm), 2.0 W (green, 540 nm), 4.3 W (red, 620 nm), 32 W (bright white) and 3.3 W (dimmed white; the Figure 1 caption gives 1.4 W), so colour and intensity are confounded and the shearwaters' spectral sensitivity was not controlled. Results: bright white -33% (95% CI 24 to 40), dimmed white -18%, blue -19.1%, green -20% (those three not significantly different from each other), red no significant effect and different from all other treatments; only one low red intensity was tested. Interval experiment: bright white 20 min -46%, 10 min -27%, 1 min no effect; dimmed white 20 min -33%, 10 min and 1 min no significant effect (8-10 control pairs per duration, lower power). The authors name neophobia as an alternative explanation and note moonlight was not fully controlled and a torch differs from real streetlights.

units: Hz (ABR hearing range; peak sensitivity 8-24 kHz in wild-caught and 8-32 kHz in laboratory-reared voles)
method: auditory brainstem responses to tone bursts at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32 and 46 kHz presented from 10 to 90 dB SPL (10 dB steps, 5 dB near threshold) through speakers placed in the ear canals; threshold taken by visual inspection as the lowest level at which wave I was detectable in both monaural stimuli
conditions: 53 adult or subadult prairie voles under ketamine/xylazine anaesthesia on a heating pad at 37 C: 33 laboratory-reared (16 males, 17 females, all adults over 60 days; from a long-established colony derived from wild Illinois voles in the 1980s and outcrossed among laboratories) and 20 wild-caught (10 males, 10 females; 16 adults, 4 subadults by body mass; live-trapped at the Kansas University Field Research Station, Nov 2024 to Mar 2025). The 1-46 kHz range is the span of the eight frequencies tested, so it is a tested range and not a measured limit, and the value pools the two groups. Wild-caught voles had significantly lower thresholds than laboratory-reared voles at 1, 4, 8, 16 and 24 kHz but not at 32 kHz, and there was no group difference at 2 and 46 kHz; click threshold 52 dB SPL (wild-caught) against 67 dB SPL (laboratory-reared); no sex differences. The paper reports no sound-attenuating chamber or ambient noise, does not mention blinding, did not control age or mating status, and notes that ABR thresholds under anaesthesia are generally 10 to 20 dB higher than behavioural thresholds in awake animals. Statistics: linear mixed-effects models with Tukey contrasts.

value: trail-following threshold of 1 fg/cm for both trail pheromone components, (3Z)-dodec-3-en-1-ol and (3Z,6Z)-dodeca-3,6-dien-1-ol, in activated workers (kept 2 h in a dish without food)
units: fg/cm of trail (lowest concentration giving active trail-following)
method: open-field Y-shaped trail-following bioassay on damp filter paper (120 degree angle between branches, moisture content 170%): a trail of extract, synthetic standard or hexane control drawn with a microlitre syringe on the 3 cm stem and/or a 5 cm branch; one termite released from a glass waiting chamber; a trail followed for more than 3.0 cm scored as active
conditions: workers from five field colonies collected at three sites around Nanjing, China, kept indoors at about 22 +/- 3 C; workers were taken at different foraging phases and 'activated' workers were held for 2 h in a Petri dish without food; each termite and each paper used once. The 1 fg/cm threshold applies to activated workers; workers taken directly in the D phase were at least ten times less sensitive to (3Z,6Z)-dodeca-3,6-dien-1-ol, and workers from the G, S and D phases preferred that component only above about 10^3, 10^4 and 10^2 fg/cm. Soldiers: 1 fg/cm for (3Z)-dodec-3-en-1-ol and 10 fg/cm for (3Z,6Z)-dodeca-3,6-dien-1-ol. The abstract gives active thresholds from 1 fg/cm to 10 pg/cm across behavioural contexts and pheromone exposure, and the two components did not act in synergy. The page text did not give the number of termites per concentration (Tables 3-7 carry the data but their rows were not returned), the full concentration series, the bioassay temperature, blinding or the order of concentrations; the applied volume is not given in the Methods.
